def factor_volume_regime_reversal_cont(df):
    """Adaptive reversal signal that blends short-term (5-day) and long-term (20-day) reversals, gated by volume regime. Uses alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime to obtain volume state flags and vol_ratio."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    is_high_vol, is_low_vol, vol_ratio = alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime(df_copy["volume"], window=20)
    short_rev = -(df_copy["close"] / df_copy["close"].shift(5) - 1)
    long_rev = -(df_copy["close"] / df_copy["close"].shift(20) - 1)
    w = np.clip(vol_ratio - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    high_mask = is_high_vol > 0
    low_mask = is_low_vol > 0
    blend_signal = w * short_rev + (1 - w) * long_rev
    factor = np.where(high_mask, short_rev, np.where(low_mask, long_rev, blend_signal))
    df_copy["factor_volume_regime_reversal_cont"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_volume_regime_reversal_cont"]
description: Volume regimes capture liquidity-driven price pressure. In high-volume states, reversals tend to be short-lived, favoring a 5-day lookback; in low-volume states, reversals develop over longer horizons, favoring a 20-day lookback. Intermediate volumes blend the two signals continuously using the relative volume ratio. This adaptive gating preserves a single continuous reversal mechanism while adjusting its speed to market liquidity conditions.
